"'''Miss You Much'''" is a song by American singer [[Janet Jackson]]. Composed by songwriters and record producers [[Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis]], it was recorded for the singer's fourth studio album, ''[[Janet Jackson's Rhythm Nation 1814]]'' (1989). As with all tracks for the album, recording took place at Lewis and Jam's Flyte Tyme Studios in [[Minneapolis]], [[Minnesota]], between 1988 and 1989. Lyrically, the song narrates a longing to reconnect with a romantic partner after time spent apart.

"Miss You Much" was released as the [[lead single]] from ''Rhythm Nation 1814'' on August 16, 1989, by [[A&M Records]]. It topped the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] singles chart, becoming the second number one hit of Jackson's career. Spending four consecutive weeks atop the chart, it was the longest running number one single of 1989. It is Jackson's third longest running Hot 100 number one, behind "[[That's the Way Love Goes (Janet Jackson song)|That's the Way Love Goes]]" (1993) and "[[All for You (Janet Jackson song)|All for You]]" (2001), which spent eight and seven weeks at number one, respectively. It also topped several ''Billboard'' composite charts, including the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot Black Singles]] and [[Dance Club Songs]] charts. Internationally, the single became a top 40 hit in all territories where it charted. It is [[RIAA certification|certified]] platinum by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA), denoting one million copies shipped in the US alone. It emerged as the number one radio airplay hit of 1989 and the second best-selling single of the year behind "[[Another Day in Paradise]]" by [[Phil Collins]]. Based on changing metrics of how chart performance is evaluated, ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine listed "Miss You Much" as Jackson's all-time biggest Hot 100 hit.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Janet Jackson's Biggest Billboard Hits|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/chart-beat/7793224/janet-jacksons-biggest-billboard-hot-100-hits|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170517002503/http://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/chart-beat/7793224/janet-jacksons-biggest-billboard-hot-100-hits|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 17, 2017|access-date=October 26, 2017}}</ref>

A music video for the song directed by [[Dominic Sena]] was produced as part of the ''[[Rhythm Nation 1814 (film)|Rhythm Nation 1814]]'' film, which aired as a 30-minute special on [[MTV]] prior to the album's release. The video for "Miss You Much" serves as the opening segment of the film and is followed by videos for two other songs from the album, "The Knowledge" and the title-track "[[Rhythm Nation]]", to form a complete narrative. Its inclusion in ''Rhythm Nation 1814'' made it part of one of the largest projects to have ever been attempted by A&M, with a budget of $1.6 million for the entire film.<ref name="Graham">{{citation|last=Graham|first=Jefferson|title=Janet takes control again in new video|newspaper=USA Today|page=1.D|date=September 14, 1989|issn=0734-7456}}</ref> As with the other two components of the film, "Miss You Much" is shot entirely in black and white. Choreographed by Jackson, Anthony Thomas and Terry Bixler, the video features a complex dance routine, culminating with a sequence where Jackson and her back-up dancers use chairs as props in conjunction with their performance. Since the video's release, numerous artists have taken inspiration from or replicated the chair routine in their own videos and live performances, including [[Britney Spears]], [[Usher (musician)|Usher]], [[Backstreet Boys]], [[NSYNC]] and [[Tinashe]].

In 1990, "Miss You Much" received [[Grammy Award]] nominations for [[Grammy Award for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance|Best Female R&B Vocal Performance]] and [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Song|Best Rhythm & Blues Song]]. It won the [[Billboard Awards|Billboard Award]] for the Top Hot 100 Single of the Year and the [[American Music Awards]] for Favorite Dance Single and Favorite R&B Single. It has been included in each of Jackson's greatest hits albums, ''[[Design of a Decade: 1986–1996]]'' (1995), ''[[Number Ones (Janet Jackson album)|Number Ones]]'' (2009) and ''[[Icon: Number Ones]]'' (2010). The song was covered in the Korean film ''[[200 Pounds Beauty]]'' (2006) and has also being sampled by artists such as [[50 Cent]].

Composed by songwriters and record producers Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, it was recorded for the singer's fourth studio album, Janet Jackson's Rhythm Nation 1814 (1989). As with all tracks for the album, recording took place at Lewis and Jam's Flyte Tyme Studios in Minneapolis, Minnesota, between 1988 and 1989. Lyrically, the song narrates a longing to reconnect with a romantic partner after time spent apart.

"Miss You Much" was released as the lead single from Rhythm Nation 1814 on August 16, 1989, by A&M Records. It topped the US Billboard Hot 100 singles chart, becoming the second number one hit of Jackson's career. Spending four consecutive weeks atop the chart, it was the longest running number one single of 1989. It is Jackson's third longest running Hot 100 number one, behind "That's the Way Love Goes" (1993) and "All for You" (2001), which spent eight and seven weeks at number one, respectively. It also topped several Billboard composite charts, including the Hot Black Singles and Dance Club Songs charts. Internationally, the single became a top 40 hit in all territories where it charted. It is certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), denoting one million copies shipped in the US alone. It emerged as the number one radio airplay hit of 1989 and the second best-selling single of the year behind "Another Day in Paradise" by Phil Collins. Based on changing metrics of how chart performance is evaluated, Billboard magazine listed "Miss You Much" as Jackson's all-time biggest Hot 100 hit.

A music video for the song directed by Dominic Sena was produced as part of the Rhythm Nation 1814 film, which aired as a 30-minute special on MTV prior to the album's release. sections.heading: Background
Chart performance
sections.wikitext: Heavy anticipation and radio [[airplay]] during the late summer allowed "Miss You Much" to debut at number 42 on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 the week of September 2, 1989. After three weeks, as "Miss You Much" entered the top-ten of Billboard Hot 100, music industry prognosticators theorized that the song would become Jackson's second number-one song on the Hot 100. However, the song started facing competition from fellow singer [[Madonna]]'s single "[[Cherish (Madonna song)|Cherish]]", which also moved into the top-five the same week.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1989-09-22/entertainment/8901150374_1_milli-vanilli-second-chart-week-disc-list|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304004405/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1989-09-22/entertainment/8901150374_1_milli-vanilli-second-chart-week-disc-list|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 4, 2014|title=London-based Milli Vanilli hits a double with No. 1 pop single and album|last=DeKnock|first=Jan|date=September 22, 1989|access-date=August 21, 2011|work=Chicago Tribune }}</ref> The popular media pitted the two women against each other and tried to create rivalry between them.<ref>{{harvnb|Dickerson|1998|p=179}}</ref> The song eventually topped on October 7, 1989, the same week "Cherish" peaked at number two.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1989/10/06/paula-abduls-forever-your-girl-took-almost-forever-to-make/|title=Paula Abdul's 'Forever Your Girl' Took Almost Forever to Make No. 1|date=October 6, 1989|last=DeKnock |first=Jan|work=Chicago Tribune |access-date=April 24, 2009}}</ref> It was the biggest airplay hit of the year, and fifth biggest overall, also peaking atop the [[Hot Dance Club Songs|Hot Dance Club Play]] and [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]] charts.<ref name="USA Today">{{Citation|last=Graham|first=Jefferson|title=Janet in command; Jackson rules her own 'Nation'; Highlights of a rhythmic life|page=1.D|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|date=December 15, 1989|issn=0734-7456}}</ref> The song was the second best-selling single of the year, behind only [[Phil Collins]]' "[[Another Day in Paradise]]". It reached number 2 in Canada and New Zealand, and the top twenty of Australia, Finland, Germany, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. It peaked within the top twenty five on the [[UK singles chart|United Kingdom singles charts]], although its accompanying album reached the top five on the [[UK Albums Chart|UK albums chart]].
sections.text: Heavy anticipation and radio airplay during the late summer allowed "Miss You Much" to debut at number 42 on the Billboard Hot 100 the week of September 2, 1989. After three weeks, as "Miss You Much" entered the top-ten of Billboard Hot 100, music industry prognosticators theorized that the song would become Jackson's second number-one song on the Hot 100. However, the song started facing competition from fellow singer Madonna's single "Cherish", which also moved into the top-five the same week. The popular media pitted the two women against each other and tried to create rivalry between them. The song eventually topped on October 7, 1989, the same week "Cherish" peaked at number two. It was the biggest airplay hit of the year, and fifth biggest overall, also peaking atop the Hot Dance Club Play and Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs charts. The song was the second best-selling single of the year, behind only Phil Collins' "Another Day in Paradise". It reached number 2 in Canada and New Zealand, and the top twenty of Australia, Finland, Germany, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. It peaked within the top twenty five on the United Kingdom singles charts, although its accompanying album reached the top five on the UK albums chart.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
[[File:Janet Jackson 3.jpg|thumb|200px|Jackson performing the song on her [[Rock Witchu Tour]] in 2008.]]

Directed by [[Dominic Sena]], choreographed by Jackson and Anthony Thomas, and filmed in August 1989 as part of the long-form ''Rhythm Nation 1814'' film, the [[black-and-white]] [[Music video|video]] for "Miss You Much" begins with dancers gathered at a pool hall, gossiping about Jackson and her boyfriend. Jackson enters the room as her dancers suddenly become quiet and look at her. One dancer asks Jackson what she has been doing lately. She jokingly responds, before demonstrating her love through song and dance. The end of the video cuts to a final dance routine performed with chairs, choreographed by Terry Bixler.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/7998755/janet-jackson-songs-best-hits-list/|title = Janet Jackson's 10 Best Songs: Critic's Picks|magazine = [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref>

The video's choreography and chair routine are regarded as iconic in popular culture. The chair routine is available on the ''Rhythm Nation Compilation'' DVD.

sections.heading: Live performances
sections.wikitext:
Jackson has performed "Miss You Much" on all of her tours, including the [[Rhythm Nation 1814 Tour]], [[janet. Tour]], [[The Velvet Rope Tour]], [[All for You Tour]], [[Rock Witchu Tour]], [[Number Ones: Up Close and Personal]], [[Unbreakable World Tour (Janet Jackson tour)|Unbreakable World Tour]], [[State of the World Tour]], and her Las Vegas Residency [[Janet Jackson: Metamorphosis]]. It was also included on her special concert series [[Janet Jackson: A Special 30th Anniversary Celebration of Rhythm Nation]] in 2019.

While promoting her second greatest hits album ''[[Number Ones (Janet Jackson album)|Number Ones]]'', the singer performed an eight-minute medley of six hits during the [[American Music Awards of 2009]]. It included "[[Control (Janet Jackson song)|Control]]", "Miss You Much", "[[What Have You Done for Me Lately]]", "[[If (Janet Jackson song)|If]]", "[[Make Me (Janet Jackson song)|Make Me]]", and finished with "[[Together Again (Janet Jackson song)|Together Again]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.janetjackson.com/story/all/janet-opens-the-american-music-awards|title=Janet Opens the American Music Awards|date=November 27, 2009|access-date=June 16, 2014|publisher=JanetJackson.com|archive-date=July 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714114244/http://www.janetjackson.com/story/all/janet-opens-the-american-music-awards|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Kaufman|first=Gil|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1626828/janet-jackson-kicks-off-american-music-awards-with-energetic-medley/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715072416/http://www.mtv.com/news/1626828/janet-jackson-kicks-off-american-music-awards-with-energetic-medley/|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 15, 2014|title=Janet Jackson Kicks Off American Music Awards With Energetic Medley|date=November 22, 2009|access-date=June 15, 2014|publisher=MTV News. Viacom}}</ref>

sections.heading: Legacy
sections.wikitext:
*[[Britney Spears]] referenced the "Miss You Much" video, and Jackson's "[[The Pleasure Principle (song)|The Pleasure Principle]]" video, for the chair routine in her "[[Stronger (Britney Spears song)|Stronger]]" video. The video's director [[Joseph Kahn (director)|Joseph Kahn]] said Spears' idea for the routine was inspired by "Janet Jackson's 'Pleasure Principle' — the iconic chair sequence in that."<ref name="Spears">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/list/473010/britney-spears-10-best-music-videos-readers-poll-results?page=0%2C2|title=Britney Spears' 10 Best Music Videos: Readers' Poll Results|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=February 19, 2011|access-date=July 13, 2013}}</ref> A review of the video commented "Ms. Spears gives us her best Janet Jackson impression ("Miss You Much") with a dizzying chair-dance routine."<ref name="Stronger">{{cite web|url=http://www.theroundtableonline.com/videos/flashback-friday-britney-spears-stronger-music-video/|title=Flashback Friday: Britney Spears "Stronger" Music Video|publisher=The Round Table Online|date=February 18, 2011|access-date=July 13, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140226160509/http://www.theroundtableonline.com/videos/flashback-friday-britney-spears-stronger-music-video/|archive-date=February 26, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* The popular [[boy band]] the [[Backstreet Boys]] performed a chair routine similar to Jackson's in their 1999 ''[[Disney Channel in Concert]]'' special to the track "[[As Long as You Love Me (Backstreet Boys song)|As Long as You Love Me]]".
* When asked if [[NSYNC]] was copying their rival the Backstreet Boys with their chair routine during "For The Girl Who Has Everything" performance from their [[Pay Per View]] concert special ''NSYNC 'N Concert'', [[Justin Timberlake]] corrects [[Rick Campanelli]] and states they got it from Janet Jackson's "Miss You Much"<ref>{{cite web |title=NSYNC on Much Live 1999 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r7FGhAnrXmI |website=YouTube}}</ref>
* During Jackson's inaugural ''[[MTV Icon]]'' tribute, "Miss You Much" was performed by [[Pink (singer)|Pink]], [[Usher (entertainer)|Usher]], and [[Mýa]] to honor Jackson. Pink notably recreated the video's iconic chair routine.
*[[VH1]]'s show ''Miss You Much'' was titled after the song.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.zap2it.com/frominsidethebox/2012/08/miss-you-much-with-catherine-reitman-will-be-nostalgic---and-creepy.html|title='Miss You Much' with Catherine Reitman will be nostalgic - and creepy|work=Zap2it|publisher=Bentley, Jean|date=August 3, 2012|access-date=February 7, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140226152023/http://blog.zap2it.com/frominsidethebox/2012/08/miss-you-much-with-catherine-reitman-will-be-nostalgic---and-creepy.html|archive-date=February 26, 2014}}</ref>
* "Miss You Much" was covered by Korean singer Youme in the South Korean comedy film ''[[200 Pounds Beauty]]'' in 2005. In the film, the song is performed by fictional Korean pop singer Ammy (Ji Seo-yun).
* [[50 Cent]]'s single "[[Follow My Lead (50 Cent song)|Follow My Lead]]", which features [[Robin Thicke]], references "Miss You Much" in the line "like Janet Jackson said, I miss you much."
* [[Akon]]'s single "[[Right Now (Na Na Na)]]" references and interpolates "Miss You Much" by quoting the line "I miss you much" using the same rhythm and melody.
* "Miss You Much" was played during an episode of [[Tori Spelling]]'s show ''[[So NoTORIous]]''.
* The song was used in one of the opening scenes of the film ''[[Ghost Dad]]'', starring [[Bill Cosby]].
* The song was used in the opening sequence of the film ''[[Southside with You]]''.
* [["Weird Al" Yankovic]] included the song's chorus in his polka medley "[[Polka Your Eyes Out]]" from his album ''[[Off the Deep End]]''.
* "Miss You Much" was featured in a dance scene in the movie ''[[Hustlers (2019 film)|Hustlers]]''. The scene featured the main cast doing choreography to the song. It was also featured in the end credits.
*The song was used in a lip sync between [[Ra'Jah O'Hara]] and [[Brooke Lynn Hytes]] on the second episode of the [[RuPaul's Drag Race All Stars (season 6)|sixth season]] of ''[[RuPaul's Drag Race All Stars|RuPaul's Drag Race: All Stars]]''.<ref>{{Citation|title=Ra'Jah O'Hara & Brooke Lynn Hytes' 'Miss You Much' Lip Sync For Your Legacy 🔥 RPDR All Stars 6|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LVXDsZ9ldaI |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211213/LVXDsZ9ldaI |archive-date=2021-12-13 |url-status=live|language=en|access-date=2021-07-20}}{{cbignore}}</ref>
*[[Leslie Cheung]] recorded a Cantonese version in his 1989 album [[Final Encounter (album)|''Final Encounter'']].
